- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; add 1–3 day lag correction to forecast decline.
- When sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.1) after a downtrend, model often underreacts; increase forecast by 1–4% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day from day 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 2+ consecutive negative values), model tends to ignore sentiment; apply sentiment-weighted adjustment: reduce forecast by 1–3% per negative sentiment unit.
